nodes.label: Gold Accounting Product
nodes.rationale: The product's accounting unit is gold rather than rial; rial is treated as a transient unit.

nodes.label: Gold-Denominated Accounting
nodes.rationale: Gold-denominated balances preserve the business's economic position through market-price changes.

nodes.label: Numeric Precision Policy
nodes.rationale: Rial and weight use bigint; money and weight are serialized as strings, and rounding is centralized in core-calc.

nodes.label: Coin as Counted Asset
nodes.rationale: Each coin type is an independent ledger dimension and must not be normalized to gold weight in storage.

nodes.label: Central-Bank Coin Bubble Rule
nodes.rationale: Only central-bank-minted coins have a bubble; bullion never has a bubble or premium.

nodes.label: Global Gold/Rial Unit Toggle
nodes.rationale: Every financial report and balance must switch between gold and rial through a user-level setting with per-page temporary override.

nodes.label: B2C Return as Second-Hand Purchase
nodes.rationale: A consumer return is a second-hand-gold purchase at the return-day rate, not a shared B2B return workflow.

nodes.label: Versioned Domain Settings
nodes.rationale: Industry values such as tax, purity, coin specifications, and labor rules are database records with validity ranges so historical documents reproduce exactly.

nodes.label: Append-Only Multi-Unit Ledger
nodes.rationale: Ledger entries are never updated or deleted; correction is a new document and a deferred database constraint enforces zero balance in each dimension per transaction.

nodes.label: Event Rate Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Every rial-to-gold conversion locks the contemporaneous market rate in the document so historical reports do not change with current prices.

nodes.label: core-calc
nodes.rationale: Pure, tested TypeScript calculations shared identically by browser and server, including the only permitted rounding location.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Scope
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 includes gold jewelry and coin sale/purchase, consumer second-hand purchase, basic inventory and reporting; bullion, silver operations, B2B returns, and other listed capabilities are excluded.

nodes.label: Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: All relevant tables carry tenant_id and use PostgreSQL Row-Level Security; write endpoints require Idempotency-Key.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Financial UI
nodes.rationale: The interface starts at 360px, uses RTL logical CSS properties, cards instead of narrow-screen tables, and 44px minimum touch targets.

nodes.label: Custom Domain Numeric Keypad
nodes.rationale: An in-app numeric keypad with domain shortcuts supports under-15-second transaction entry without reliance on the system keyboard.

nodes.label: Graphify Maintenance Workflow
nodes.rationale: Use graph.json first for structural questions, run graphify . --update after each completed task, save useful results, and reflect on stale lessons at session start.
